task.title: T10 re-run: verify the closure, TLS and the operator console on a real relay after T16
task.description:
Independently verify flow 002 on the post-T16 tree. This is the fourth attempt at T10 and the earlier verdicts are NOT credited retroactively — judge AC1..AC6 yourself on this tree.

History you need, stated so you know where the bodies are buried. Attempt 2 found T10-F-001, a truncated contact-import re-walk that permanently lost a message; T14 fixed it by introducing a durable re-walk position `cli:mailbox-rewalk`. Attempt 3 confirmed that fix by measurement but found T10R3-F-001: the re-walk was not crash-safe, because `takeMailboxRewalk()` deleted the position before the walk and it was written back only on return, so an interruption anywhere inside the walk — Ctrl-C was enough — silently and permanently lost the message. The orchestrator declined to accept that as a residual. T15 wrote the RED tests and T16 has now implemented the fix.

T16's claim, which you must check rather than believe: the shape is now peek-and-advance. `requestMailboxRewalk()` writes the head position at `contact import`; the page loop calls `keepMailboxRewalk(next_cursor)` once per page the walk received and FULLY judged, in the same place `read_through` is computed; and the new `finishMailboxRewalk()` clears it in exactly one place, only when `next_cursor === null`. T16 argues there is no window at all, because each page is a single store transaction replacing P(k-1) with P(k), so the store holds P(k-1) before the commit and P(k) after and never holds nothing.

The trap, which you must confirm was not taken: delete-before-the-walk was deliberate, per finding T6-F-004 — a position surviving its own SUCCESSFUL walk restarts every later poll at the same place and reinstates the entire flooding class this flow exists to close. Two guards pin it (`rewalk-crash-safety` case 4, and `flood-closure` RED-4b). Verify by measurement that a completed re-walk is genuinely not repeated, rather than reading the guards' names.

T16 also applied the shape/range split to the ack route (shape before authorisation, range only after `VerifyMessageSignature`) and converged `RelayClient` and `parseClientConfig` on one loopback predicate in the new `apps/cli/src/transport/loopback.ts`.

Sweep the coverage bound T15 and T16 both recorded as a residual (T15-F-003): the crash-safety suite exercises ONE interruption point — a held page 3 — and ONE ciphertext regime, 4 bytes. Interruptions inside `accept()`, between the last page's commits and the clear, inside `ackPending()`, and the maximum-size-ciphertext regime are argued correct but were never measured. Measure them.
task.scope: apps/cli, apps/relay, the flow 002 artifacts, and docs/requirements/echolet-cli-prototype; loopback only

acceptance_criteria: AC1: The flooding closure is chosen by a written design task that names what it closes, what it does not close, and why the alternatives were rejected.

AC2: Against the real relay binary, the probe that previously wedged a mailbox with 4 self-published identities and 49 maximum-size envelopes no longer prevents delivery of a legitimate message, and the new attacker cost is measured and stated. If the result is a bound rather than a closure, it is reported as a bound and not as a fix.

AC3: A legitimate two-party exchange, offline delivery, byte-identical exact retry and deduplication all still pass on the real relay after the change, with no pre-existing test weakened, skipped or deleted.

AC4: A relay reachable on a non-loopback address serves HTTPS, and the CLI completes the full acceptance scenario against it from a different machine. The 'different machine' half cannot be established from loopback and you are forbidden to touch the remote hosts — report it as partial with that reason rather than as met or failed.

AC5: The operator console drives a local CLI, shows profiles, queues, history, rejections and relay health, and never receives, stores or transmits a store key or private key material. This is demonstrated by evidence, not asserted.
AC6: The console displays, on its own surface, that this is an unaudited prototype not suitable for sensitive communication.

T10R3-F-001 is closed: interrupt a recovery poll with SIGINT and with SIGKILL, at SEVERAL different points — inside the page request, inside acceptance, between the last page's commit and the clear, and inside the acknowledgement — and show the message is still delivered by a later poll without a second `contact import`. State the first configuration, if any, at which a message is still lost.

The T6-F-004 property still holds by your own measurement: a re-walk that completed is not repeated, later ordinary polls do not restart at the head, and the cost of three ordinary polls after a completed re-walk stays bounded.

T10R3-F-002 is closed: the lifetime envelope count is not answerable on the ack route to a caller whose signature does not verify, including one holding a genuine contact-card `device_id`; re-run the binary search yourself and report how many distinct answers it can distinguish.
T10R3-F-003 is closed: `RelayClient` and `parseClientConfig` agree on every URL you can construct, including hostnames a `/^127\./` prefix rule wrongly admits, and genuine loopback still works.

The full matrix is re-run on this tree by you: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e`, and `go -C apps/relay test ./...` untagged, with `-race` and with `-race -tags relayv2`. Report exact counts, exit codes and data-race counts.
Repository integrity is verified by SHA-256 over tracked files, and every test file T15 wrote or touched is shown unchanged by T16.

context_refs.summary: Attempt 3's report: the measurements that confirmed T14, and the three findings T16 has now fixed.
T16's own account of the peek-and-advance shape, the ack split, the loopback predicate and six residuals. A claim to check, not evidence.
The closure design and the residuals R-1..R-8 written before implementation.
The orchestrator's rulings, including why the re-walk floor stays local and why RED-4's cursorless line was re-stated.
The reproduction runbook whose commands were executed against the real relay and the real dist/cli.js.

constraints: Do not modify any source, test, documentation or flow file. This is a read-and-measure task; your only writes are your two deliverables and scratch files under /tmp.
Do not touch the remote hosts geekom or depr, and do not open any non-loopback listener.
Do not weaken, skip, delete or filter any test to obtain a green result. Report a failure as a failure.
Do not print plaintext, ciphertext, store keys, profile keys, private key material or HTTP request bodies into any log, report or terminal output.
Every text or symbol search goes through `keryx ctx rg`, never a bare rg or grep; route commands and large logs through `keryx ctx run` / `keryx ctx read`.
Verify integrity by SHA-256, never mtime — files in this tree have been touched with byte-identical content.

`bash -lc` on this machine starts Node v22.12.0, which lacks `node:sqlite` and makes packages/session-node fail to collect in a way indistinguishable from broken code. Use the default non-login interpreter, v26.5.0, and report the version you measured on.
Finding a real defect is a successful outcome for this task. Do not soften a verdict to let the flow proceed.

provenance.source_request: T16 reports all eight handover REDs green and the full matrix clean; T10 must be re-run rather than credited, and must sweep the coverage bound T15-F-003 that both T15 and T16 recorded.
